intro: You are given distributed traces from an online-shop microservice system in the style of the OpenTelemetry demo, with services such as frontend, cart, checkout, currency, payment, shipping, quote, email, product-catalog, recommendation, ad, accounting, fraud-detection, valkey-cart and flagd. Requests are grouped into {n} request classes, each defined by an endpoint, a client and a region, and each class contains {k} sampled traces. Every span row has the fields span_id, parent_id (- for the root span), service, operation, start_us, duration_us and status. Your job: for every request class, find the operation (identified by its service and operation name together) with the largest mean self time, under the rules below.
rules: - The self time of a span is its duration minus the part of its own time interval [start_us, start_us + duration_us) covered by its direct children; children that run in parallel are counted once (take the union of the children's intervals), and any part of a child that lies outside the parent's interval does not count (asynchronous consumers can start after their parent has ended).
- A trace whose root span has status ERROR is excluded from all averages; status values of other spans do not matter.
- An operation's self time in a trace is the total self time of all its spans in that trace (an operation can appear several times in one trace).
- An operation's mean self time in a class is the average, over the class's non-excluded traces, of its self time per trace.

- The answer for a class is the operation with the largest mean self time. Operations are identified as "<service> <operation>", for example "cart oteldemo.CartService/GetCart". The slowest span by total duration is usually a parent and is often not the answer.

tools.list_classes: Lists the class ids with their endpoint, client and region, paged, returning at most 100 per call.
tools.list_traces: Lists the trace ids of one class, each with its root span's status and duration and the span count.
tools.get_trace: Returns all spans of one trace as rows: span_id | parent_id | service | operation | start_us | duration_us | status.

answer: The final answer is one JSON object mapping every class id to its operation, written as "<service> <operation>"; for example {example}.
score: The score is the fraction of classes answered correctly.
unit_prompt: Analyse exactly one request class, {cid}, using the same tools (list_classes, list_traces, get_trace) and the rules placed at {rules}. Fetch the traces of the class, apply the self-time and exclusion rules, compute the mean self time of every operation over the class's non-excluded traces, and determine the operation with the largest mean self time. End your reply with exactly one final line of the literal form UNIT | {cid2} | <service> <operation>.
